requirements.quote:
All communications inside of the domain protocol are carried in a single
format called a message.  The top level format of message is divided
into 5 sections (some of which are empty in certain cases) shown below:

    +---------------------+
    |        Header       |
    +---------------------+
    |       Question      | the question for the name server
    +---------------------+
    |        Answer       | RRs answering the question
    +---------------------+
    |      Authority      | RRs pointing toward an authority
    +---------------------+
    |      Additional     | RRs holding additional information
    +---------------------+
requirements.condition: For the top-level structure of a domain protocol message.
requirements.required_behavior: Define the five sections Header, Question, Answer, Authority, and Additional; some sections may be empty in applicable cases.
requirements.why_checkable: The message data structure and wire layout expose the defined section set.

requirements.quote:
+---------------------+
    |        Header       |

    +---------------------+
    |        Answer       | RRs answering the question

    +---------------------+
    |      Additional     | RRs holding additional information
    +---------------------+
requirements.condition: For the top-level wire layout of a domain protocol message.
requirements.required_behavior: Order the sections as Header, Question, Answer, Authority, then Additional.
requirements.why_checkable: Serialized messages can be inspected for the specified section ordering.

requirements.quote: The header section is always present.
requirements.why_checkable: A serialized message can be checked for its header.

requirements.quote:
The header section is always present.  The header includes fields that
specify which of the remaining sections are present, and also specify
whether the message is a query or a response, a standard query or some
other opcode, etc.
requirements.condition: For the header of a domain protocol message.
requirements.required_behavior: Include fields that specify which remaining sections are present.
requirements.why_checkable: Header fields and the indicated non-header sections can be compared.

requirements.quote:
The names of the sections after the header are derived from their use in
standard queries.  The question section contains fields that describe a
question to a name server.  These fields are a query type (QTYPE), a
query class (QCLASS), and a query domain name (QNAME).  The last three
sections have the same format: a possibly empty list of concatenated
resource records (RRs).  The answer section contains RRs that answer the
question; the authority section contains RRs that point toward an
authoritative name server; the additional records section contains RRs
which relate to the query, but are not strictly answers for the
question.
requirements.condition: For the answer section in a standard-query response.
requirements.required_behavior: Place resource records answering the question in the answer section.
requirements.why_checkable: The response-construction logic and answer records can be compared with the question.
